from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Dimensions distinguish lines from squares.",
            "Can a one-dimensional line fill space?",
            "Mapping the interval to the square."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuitive Paradox: Can a line fill a square?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        label_l = Text("L", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        square = Square(side_length=2.0, color=WHITE)
        label_s = Text("S", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # Initial positions
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'E2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_l, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(line), Write(label_l))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        # Transform line to square
        # Need to re-position square and label
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_s, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(line, square), 
            ReplacementTransform(label_l, label_s)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Show filling
        dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        self.add(dot)
        dot.move_to(square.get_left())
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, square), run_time=3)
        self.play(square.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("The Peano Curve: Construction through Iteration",

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Beauty of Convergent Complexity", [
            "Finite rules generate infinite complexity.",
            "Topology bridges lines and squares.",
            "Mathematical beauty emerges from recursion."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        recursive_tree = VGroup(
            *[Line(ORIGIN, UP * 0.5).rotate(i * 360/8 * DEGREES) for i in range(8)]
        ).set_color(BLUE)
        
        final_square = Square(side_length=2, color=ORANGE).set_fill(ORANGE, opacity=0.3)
        paradox_dim = Text("1D vs 2D", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(recursive_tree, 'B3', 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(recursive_tree))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(recursive_tree))
        self.place_at_grid(final_square, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(final_square))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(paradox_dim, 'E4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(paradox_dim))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Space-Filling Curves: Bridging the Finite and the Infinite
outline.target_audience: University students with a foundational knowledge of geometry and sequences

sections.title: The Intuitive Paradox: Can a line fill a square?
sections.content: Introduce the standard definition of dimension. Ask: can a 1D line ever occupy every point in a 2D square? Establish the prerequisite: the concept of mapping a unit interval [0,1] onto a unit square [0,1]x[0,1].
sections.example: Visualize a piece of string; try to pack it into a square box so no space is left empty.

sections.title: The Peano Curve: Construction through Iteration
sections.content: Explain the step-by-step recursive process. Start with a single line segment, divide it into 9 squares, and connect the centers. Show how the curve becomes increasingly complex as the number of iterations (n) approaches infinity.
sections.example: An animation of the Peano curve evolving: from a simple 'S' shape to a dense, labyrinth-like web that looks like a solid block.

sections.title: The Infinite Limit: Breaking Dimensional Intuition
sections.content: Address the relationship between finite steps and infinite limits. Explain that while any finite iteration is still a 1D curve, the limit object is 'space-filling' because it passes through every single coordinate in the unit square.
sections.example: A 'Digital Ant' traversing the curve: as iterations increase, the ant visits every pixel in the square, eventually covering the entire canvas.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Convergent Complexity
sections.content: Synthesize the bridge between finite mathematics (the discrete steps) and infinite mathematics (the continuous limit). Emphasize that the space-filling curve is a continuous mapping that collapses the distinction between 1D and 2D topology.
sections.example: A cosmic fractal zoom: visualizing how finite rules generate infinite complexity, appearing in nature like the veins of a leaf or the circuitry of a high-density microchip.
